renders._yaml:
- component: figure
  id: spikein_factor_bar
  title: Spike-in scale factor per sample
  description: |-
    Each bar is a library: the factor its coverage is multiplied by, the normalisation constant divided by the pairs aligned to the spike-in genome. It answers how much each library is scaled before samples are compared.
    How to read: a larger factor means fewer spike-in pairs, so the library is scaled up. Factors that differ widely between replicates of one condition point to uneven spike-in addition, so consider another normalisation.
    Lines and annotations: the constant is 10000, the default normalisation_c of nf-core/cutandrun, and no cut-off is drawn.
     The dashed line is the median scale factor of this table, a reference
    computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of Bowtie 2.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/cutandrun/master/nextflow_schema.json
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: scale_factor
    color: sample
    labels:
      sample: Library
      scale_factor: Scale factor
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: scale_factor

- component: figure
  id: spikein_depth_scatter
  title: Target depth against spike-in depth
  description: |-
    Each point is a library: the pairs aligned to the spike-in genome on the horizontal axis and to the target genome on the vertical axis. It answers whether the two depths move together, as they do when the spike-in amount is constant.
    How to read: libraries of one antibody should lie along a rising band. A point off the band has an unusual amount of spike-in for its depth. With few libraries the pattern is weak, so read it with the scale factor bars.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/cutandrun/master/docs/output.md
  visu_type: scatter
  dict_kwargs:
    x: spikein_aligned
    y: target_aligned
    color: sample
    labels:
      spikein_aligned: Pairs aligned to the spike-in genome
      target_aligned: Pairs aligned to the target genome
      sample: Library

- component: card
  title: Scale factor
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median spike-in scale factor, and the box shows how the libraries spread. It answers how large the normalisation adjustment is.
    How to read: a tight box means the libraries hold similar spike-in amounts. A long whisker marks a library that will be scaled far more than the others.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/cutandrun/master/nextflow_schema.json
  column: scale_factor
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median scale factor, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Spike-in pairs
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of pairs aligned to the spike-in genome, and the bars rank the libraries with most. It answers how much spike-in material the run holds.
    How to read: a library with far fewer pairs than the others will get a large scale factor. The nf-core/cutandrun documentation asks for more than 1000 spike-in reads per sample to rise above noise, so use the next card to check.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/cutandrun/master/docs/output.md
  column: spikein_aligned
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: sample
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: total pairs aligned to the spike-in, with the richest libraries ranked

- component: card
  title: Lowest spike-in depth
  description: |-
    The hero number is the lowest number of pairs aligned to the spike-in genome in any library. It answers whether every library holds enough spike-in to be normalised.
    How to read: higher is better. A library under the line has spike-in too low to separate from noise, so another normalisation, such as the read count, is safer.
    Lines and annotations: the line is 1000 spike-in reads, the level the nf-core/cutandrun documentation gives for a spike-in signal above noise. The table counts pairs, so it is a close approximation.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/cutandrun/master/docs/output.md
  column: spikein_aligned
  aggregation: min
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 1000.0
  threshold_direction: min
  caption: lowest spike-in pair count, with the median and highest

- component: card
  title: Target alignment rate
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average of Bowtie 2's overall alignment rate against the target genome, in percent and shown against 100. It answers how much of each library maps to the genome of interest.
    How to read: a low rate points to contamination, a wrong reference or poor reads. Bowtie 2 reports the rate but defines no pass level, so none is drawn.
    Source: https://bowtie-bio.sourceforge.net/bowtie2/manual.shtml
  column: target_align_rate
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: gauge
  coverage_max: 100.0
  caption: average percent aligned to the target genome, with the lowest and highest

- component: table
  title: Spike-in factors per library
  description: |-
    Each row is a library with its read pairs, pairs aligned to the target and spike-in genomes with their rates, the spike-in fraction and the scale factor. It answers the exact numbers behind the normalisation.
    How to read: sort by scale factor to find the libraries scaled most.
